newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset sees five pct rise in 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset sees five pct rise in 1997 turnover.

text.p: Italian multi-media group Mediaset said on Thursday it had firmly set its sights on becoming Italy's second largest fixed line phone operator through its involvement with British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro in the Albacom venture.

"In fixed line telephony we propose to become the second operator, we have a clear plan to be the second operator in importance after Telecom Italia," Mediaset Managing Director Ubaldo Livolsi said in an interview.
Livolsi said the entry of France Telecom as a partner in Infostrada, a rival telecom venture established in 1995 with Olivetti and Bell Atlantic, did not pose an immediate threat to Albacom.
"It's true that Infostrada is there but after the agreement with France Telecom they will need time to become operative. We are calmly convinced we can face up to the challenge," he said.
France Telecom said on Wednesday it would buy a 49 percent stake in Infostrada, leaving Olivetti and Bell in joint control of 51 percent of the venture.
Fixed line telecommunications are dominated by Telecom Italia , which formerly enjoyed a state monopoly.
Livolsi made the remarks after Mediaset announced a slight fall in net profit for 1996 to 445.3 billion lire ($268.1 million) from 454.6 billion the previous year, reflecting a higher tax charge.
Pretax profit rose sharply to 835.4 billion lire in 1996 from 578.1 billion, boosted by increased revenues from advertising and a hold-down on operating costs within the group.
The group announced it was increasing the dividend to 195 lire from 175 lire in 1995.
Mediaset also reported a strong rise in advertising revenue from its Publitalia 80 subsidiary which rose 10.4 percent in the first quarter of 1996.
Livolsi said he expected Mediaset to achieve an increase in 1997 turnover of possibly more than five percent, helped by the rise in advertising revenue.
"This year the market is growing strongly and for 1997 we have budgeted for nominal growth of over five percent for the whole year and of 2.5 percent in real terms," said Livolsi in an interview.
"Overall 1997 profitability in view of the first months looks positive and in line with expectations. We are optimistic for results," said Livolsi.

Livolsi said the exercise by Mediaset of an option to raise its stake in Spanish broadcaster Telecinco "has given us a shareholding which will allow us to consolidate a good profit. The expectations for 1997 are excellent."
He later told analysts the company was looking to Latin America for possible opportunities in television through Telecinco.
Mediaset and its Albacom partners would look closely at the terms of a competitive tender for a third mobile phone operator in Italy before deciding whether to make a bid.
The government is expected later this year to invite bids to operate a PCN network in competition with Omnitel and TIM which both run GSM systems.

"We are carrying out simulations and studies with our partners but not to enter would not be our decision alone. We await the tender with impatience because much will depend on how it is formulated," Livolsi said.
State-owned operator Telecom Italia Mobile and Omnitel -- a venture led by Olivetti and launched in 1996 -- are currently the only two licensed mobile phone operators in Italy.
"The more time passes and the more the present competitors consolidate their position, something which risks making a third player non-competitive," said Livolsi.

Mediaset was hoping for even-handed treatment from the government, which is drafting legislation to set up a regulatory authority for telecoms and establishing antitrust rules in television broadcasting.

Following a constitutional Court ruling in 1994 that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels, Mediaset is expected to have to trasnfer one of its three terrestrial channels to satellite transmission.
"We are convinced that it would be far-fetched to hit at a company like Mediaset which is financially strong, has good managers and is growing," he said. ($ = 1660 Italian Lire)
